functions.subDef: Position primary surfaces (ailerons/spoilers, stabiliser/elevators, split rudder) to command pitch, roll and yaw; inputs: pilot inceptor, autopilot, air/inertial data from AVI; processing: three dissimilar FBW computers voting; outputs: surface position, envelope-protection status to AVI. Independence note: mechanical reversion path to stabiliser trim and lower rudder retained (SDD §5.3.2).
functions.funcDef: Aircraft behaviour of positioning aerodynamic surfaces to achieve commanded flight path and attitude across the envelope, including engine-out and blade-loaded cases (SDD §5.3.1).

functions.subDef: Extend/retract Fowler flaps and full-span slats to achieve required lift at low speed; inputs: crew/system command; processing: two independent power drive units through common torque shaft with asymmetry brakes; outputs: high-lift position to performance computation. Independence note: common torque shaft is a recorded commonality (SDD §5.3.2).
functions.funcDef: Aircraft behaviour of positioning aerodynamic surfaces to achieve commanded flight path and attitude across the envelope, including engine-out and blade-loaded cases (SDD §5.3.1).

functions.subDef: Gear supports the aircraft and spreads footprint pressure to the level semi-prepared surfaces require; inputs: hydraulic A for retract/extend, free-fall alternate; processing: bogie/tyre flotation sizing; outputs: gear position, weight-on-wheels to many consumers. functions.subDef: Carbon multi-disc braking decelerates the aircraft within the landing distance requirement; inputs: HYD B normal / HYD A alternate / accumulator emergency, brake commands; processing: electrically signalled, hydraulically actuated, per-wheel-pair anti-skid; outputs: brake temperature to AVI. Independence note: dual hydraulic supply plus accumulator reserve (SDD §5.6.2).

functions.funcDef: Aircraft behaviour of supporting the aircraft on the ground, absorbing landing/taxi loads on prepared and semi-prepared surfaces, and providing braking and directional control (SDD §5.6.1).

functions.subName: Restrain the payload through all load cases

functions.subDef: Supply conditioned air to the two zones; inputs: engine/APU bleed through cross-bleed manifold, ram air, electrical power; processing: two air-cycle packs, either from either side; outputs: conditioned air, bleed demand to IPS (SDD §5.9.2).

functions.subDef: Acquire and display flight, navigation and system data; inputs: data from every aircraft system, air/inertial and navigation signals, electrical power; processing: three display processors on dual networks, three reference units, two flight-management computers; outputs: displays to crew, commands to autopilot/autothrottle, recorded parameters. functions.subName: Extinguish fire in engine and APU zones

functions.subDef: Supply oxygen to four mask stations for the required diversion duration; inputs: two HP cylinders on a crossover manifold, cabin-altitude signal from ECS, crew donning action, DC power for indication only; processing: demand regulators independent per mask; outputs: oxygen to masks, cylinder pressure and low-pressure alerting to flight deck. fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded thrust change on one or more engines with no crew command
fha.effAc: Uncommanded thrust change produces a trajectory/energy deviation and, if from an outboard engine at the 28 m moment arm, a yaw/roll upset that must be countered by the crew; recoverable while within rudder authority.
fha.effCrew: Crew detects deviation via engine/flight instruments and alerting, retards or shuts down the affected engine and re-trims; increased workload during recovery.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect beyond flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: An uncommanded outboard thrust change at 0.35 semi-span drives an asymmetric upset; if worst-case timing/phase gives a large reduction in safety margins with high crew workload to arrest divergence, effects support Hazardous. Confirm against FCS directional-control sizing. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected slow thrust drift on one or more engines below the crew-detection threshold
fha.effAc: Slow, sub-threshold thrust drift; the crew takes no action and continues normally. Aircraft experiences a gradual energy/asymmetry error that, if it accumulates undetected, could reduce margins.
fha.effCrew: By definition below the crew-detection threshold: crew unaware and takes no corrective action.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect beyond flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground an aircraft-level effect magnitude from the SDD alone: whether an undetected sub-threshold drift stays benign or accumulates to a margin reduction depends on the drift rate, the detection threshold and the exposure time before any consequence — none of which are given. Needs engineering data to classify.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of propulsive thrust with directional-control asymmetry, within available control authority
fha.effAc: Loss of one engine (worst case outboard at 28 m moment arm) yields asymmetric thrust and reduced performance; aircraft is designed to continue to a suitable aerodrome after loss of any one engine at or after V1, so trajectory is maintainable with rudder input.
fha.effCrew: Crew identifies the failed engine, applies rudder/re-trims, secures the engine per procedure and diverts; increased workload but manageable.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect beyond flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Single-engine partial loss within control authority is a design dispatch case (continue to a suitable aerodrome after loss of any one engine): a significant reduction in margins/performance and a significant increase in crew workload support Major. Confirm the worst applicable phase. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of propulsive thrust with asymmetry beyond available directional-control authority
fha.effAc: Asymmetric thrust exceeds rudder authority, giving uncontrollable yaw/roll divergence and potential loss of controlled flight; e.g. loss of a second engine on the same side is outside the design dispatch case.
fha.effCrew: Crew cannot arrest the directional divergence with available authority; recovery not assured.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect beyond flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Asymmetry beyond directional-control authority implies loss of controlled flight; the SDD flags loss of a second engine on the same side as outside the design dispatch case and a condition to be studied. Uncontrollable divergence supports Catastrophic. Confirm the specific combinations that exceed authority against FCS sizing. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of propulsive thrust generation (all four engines)
fha.effAc: Aircraft loses all thrust; unpowered flight only, forced descent/off-airport landing outside the semi-prepared strip case.
fha.effCrew: Crew must attempt engine-out relight and a power-off forced landing; extreme workload with no thrust restoration path certain.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only exposed. Outcome is loss of the airplane.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Total loss of propulsive thrust in any phase leaves no means of sustained flight; effect is loss of the airplane. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded reverse thrust deployment in flight
fha.effAc: Uncommanded in-flight reverser deployment on an inboard engine produces large asymmetric thrust and drag; potential loss of control depending on speed and altitude.
fha.effCrew: Sudden asymmetry demands immediate directional-control and thrust-management response; very high workload, control margin depends on airspeed.
fha.effPax: Flight crew only exposed; potential loss of the airplane if control cannot be recovered.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — SDD states reverser deployment is inhibited in flight by weight-on-wheels and radio-altimeter agreement with a mechanical sleeve lock, so the residual in-flight effect after those protections is not derivable from the function definition alone; controllability outcome (recoverable asymmetry vs loss of control) needs FCS directional-control sizing to classify — cannot commit severity.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Asymmetric reverse thrust on ground deceleration
fha.effAc: One inboard reverser producing thrust the other does not yields a directional-control upset during the ground roll on a semi-prepared strip; potential runway departure.
fha.effCrew: Crew must counter yaw with steering/braking during rollout on an unprepared surface; increased workload during a critical deceleration phase.
fha.effPax: Flight crew only exposed.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Only two inboard engines carry reversers; the directional-control consequence of a single-side reverser asymmetry on a 1,800 m semi-prepared strip against ~1,080 m predicted rollout depends on steering/braking authority retained and surface friction, which the aircraft-function definition does not establish — cannot commit severity.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of ground deceleration thrust
fha.effAc: Reduced reverse-thrust deceleration lengthens the ground roll; the 1,800 m requirement against ~1,080 m predicted rollout carries the deceleration margin, and wheel braking remains available.
fha.effCrew: Crew relies more on wheel braking; some increase in workload and attention during rollout.
fha.effPax: Flight crew only exposed.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Reverse thrust is one contributor to ground deceleration alongside wheel braking; whether a partial reverse loss reduces the stated stopping margin to a safety-significant degree depends on the braking/flotation deceleration budget (1,800 m vs ~1,080 m) which is a performance analysis, not derivable from the function definition — cannot commit severity.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of ground deceleration thrust (reverse)
fha.effAc: No reverse-thrust contribution to the ground roll; deceleration relies entirely on wheel braking against the 1,800 m requirement vs ~1,080 m predicted rollout margin, on a semi-prepared surface.
fha.effCrew: Crew uses full wheel braking for the rollout; the stopping-distance margin is consumed further, particularly on a degraded surface.
fha.effPax: Flight crew only exposed.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Complete loss of reverse thrust is a total loss of one deceleration means but wheel braking remains; whether the residual braking-only stopping distance stays inside 1,800 m on a semi-prepared strip (and thus the reduction in safety margin) is a performance/landing-distance determination not established by the function definition — cannot commit severity.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of reverse thrust unannunciated at deceleration onset
fha.effAc: Ground deceleration proceeds on wheel braking alone with no reverse-thrust contribution; on the sizing case (1,800 m semi-prepared requirement vs ~1,080 m predicted rollout) the residual margin is consumed by degraded/wet/contaminated braking, with risk of overrun on the semi-prepared strip.
fha.effCrew: Crew receives no annunciation and continues the landing rollout normally, discovering the deficit late through deceleration feel; increased workload and reduced time to react (heavier braking, directional management).
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effects grounded but severity not committed: reversers are fitted to inboard engines only and the SDD does not quantify the braking-only stopping distance on a semi-prepared surface, so it cannot be shown whether the ~720 m margin absorbs the loss (Major) or is exhausted into an overrun (Hazardous). Confirm the braking-only performance case before classifying.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous attitude response to crew command
fha.effAc: Aircraft responds in pitch, roll or yaw differently from the commanded attitude, degrading control of trajectory; erroneous response near the ground or in the engine-out/blade-loaded directional case can exceed recoverable margins.
fha.effCrew: Crew must detect the discrepancy between command and response and react; high workload to diagnose and counter an incorrectly responding control law, potentially with degraded-law annunciation.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Severity not committed: an erroneous attitude response ranges from a nuisance offset to a loss of control depending on the magnitude of the error, the axis, and the flight phase — none of which the SDD quantifies (it states control authority and dissimilar FCC architecture but not failure-effect magnitude). Provide the worst-case error amplitude/phase before classifying.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded attitude motion with no command
fha.effAc: Aircraft develops pitch, roll or yaw motion with no crew input, driving the trajectory away from the intended flight path; an uncommanded excursion at low altitude or high speed can exceed recoverable margins.
fha.effCrew: Crew must recognise the uncommanded divergence and arrest it against the control system; high workload, and the mechanical reversion path is a survivable but degraded fallback only with all three FCCs lost.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Severity not committed: the aircraft effect of an uncommanded excursion spans Major to Catastrophic depending on divergence rate, axis and phase and on whether crew or the voting architecture arrests it in time — the SDD gives architecture and reversion but no excursion-rate or recovery-margin data. Provide worst-case divergence magnitude/rate before classifying.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected slow uncommanded attitude divergence below crew threshold
fha.effAc: A slow attitude divergence develops below the crew-detection threshold, gradually displacing the trajectory; because it is undetected it is not arrested and can accumulate toward a significant excursion or an out-of-trim state before it becomes apparent.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue their duties normally and take no action regarding it (unaware condition); recovery, when the state finally becomes apparent, occurs from a larger displacement with less available margin.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Severity not committed: the outcome of an undetected slow divergence depends on how far the state accumulates before it becomes apparent and on the margin remaining at that point — data the SDD does not provide (it describes monitoring/voting but not the divergence rate versus detection threshold). Provide the accumulation-versus-detection case before classifying.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of attitude control authority within controllable limits
fha.effAc: Reduced control authority in one or more axes; aircraft remains controllable but with reduced safety margins and degraded control law annunciated to the crew.
fha.effCrew: Increased workload to maintain the intended trajectory within the retained authority; degraded-law procedures applied.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect (flight crew only).
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Effects stated describe reduced control authority within controllable limits with increased crew workload but no loss of continued safe flight — a significant reduction in safety margins and significant increase in crew workload. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of attitude control authority beyond controllable limits
fha.effAc: Retained control authority insufficient to maintain the intended trajectory in one or more axes; the aircraft cannot be kept within its safe operating envelope.
fha.effCrew: Crew unable to arrest departure from controlled flight with the authority remaining.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect (flight crew only).
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: By definition beyond controllable limits: the retained authority cannot maintain controlled flight, driving loss of the airplane. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of attitude control authority
fha.effAc: No means of controlling aircraft attitude in pitch, roll or yaw; loss of controlled flight.
fha.effCrew: Crew has no means to control the trajectory.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect (flight crew only).
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Complete loss of attitude control authority yields loss of controlled flight and loss of the airplane. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Asymmetric high-lift deployment
fha.effAc: Asymmetric lift and rolling moment during low-speed flight; degraded controllability and altered stall characteristics at the phases where high-lift is in use.
fha.effCrew: Increased workload to counter the asymmetry; asymmetry annunciation and associated procedure.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect (flight crew only).
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The provided function definition ("provide high-lift for low-speed flight") states what high-lift achieves but not the aircraft's controllability margin against a given asymmetry magnitude; whether asymmetric deployment is within or beyond controllable limits — and therefore Hazardous vs Catastrophic — requires the flight-control asymmetry-brake coverage and controllability analysis, which is not in the provided inputs.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded high-lift movement
fha.effAc: High-lift surfaces move without command, changing lift and drag and potentially exceeding the surface's placard speed if it occurs at high speed; possible structural overload of the high-lift devices and altered handling.
fha.effCrew: Increased workload to detect and arrest the uncommanded movement; associated procedure.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect (flight crew only).
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The provided function definition does not establish the speed/phase envelope at which uncommanded movement could occur relative to high-lift structural placards, nor the controllability consequence; the aircraft effect cannot be pinned to a single severity without the high-lift structural limit and speed-envelope data, which are not in the provided inputs.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected asymmetric high-lift deployment below the detection threshold
fha.effAc: Asymmetric lift/drag across the span produces an uncommanded rolling and yawing moment during low-speed flight; below the asymmetry-detection threshold the asymmetry brakes and crew alerting do not engage, so the condition persists and the aircraft departs the intended flight path if not countered.
fha.effCrew: No annunciation; crew must recognise the anomaly from handling cues alone and apply corrective control, increasing workload at a low-speed, low-margin phase.
fha.effPax: Hold is unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effects point to an uncommanded roll/yaw at low speed with no annunciation, but the SDD does not state the magnitude of asymmetry that remains below the detection threshold nor the resulting reduction in safety margin, so I cannot ground whether the residual effect is Major (significant reduction in margins) or Hazardous (large reduction). Missing: the sub-threshold asymmetry limit and its effect on controllability. Left empty pending that input.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous ground support/flotation configuration indication
fha.effAc: Ground support/flotation status (e.g. gear down-and-locked/configuration) is indicated incorrectly to the crew; the aircraft's actual ground support state may differ from what is displayed, potentially leading to a configuration mismatch at touchdown or ground operation on a semi-prepared surface.
fha.effCrew: Crew acts on erroneous configuration indication; consequence depends on whether the true state is safe or unsafe and on the phase of ground operation.
fha.effPax: Hold is unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The failure condition is a misleading indication, but the aircraft-level effect depends on the true underlying ground-support state and on crew response, neither of which the function definition establishes at aircraft level. The SDD gives dual independent downlock sensing but does not state the consequence of an erroneous indication. Missing: the true state driving the effect and its controllability. Left empty rather than reaching for a value.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected loss of ground support configuration integrity
fha.effAc: Ground support/flotation configuration is compromised without annunciation, so the crew continues normal duties assuming an intact ground-support state; the actual capability to support the aircraft on a semi-prepared surface may be lost or degraded, with potential for collapse or excessive footprint loading at touchdown or during ground operation.
fha.effCrew: No annunciation; crew takes no corrective action and is surprised by the ground-support anomaly at or after touchdown.
fha.effPax: Hold is unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — An undetected loss of ground-support integrity at landing on a semi-prepared strip could be severe, but the aircraft-level outcome (structural collapse vs degraded flotation vs recoverable) is not established by the function definition, and the SDD does not state the consequence of the loss. Missing: the specific integrity mode lost and the resulting aircraft outcome/controllability. Left empty rather than presuming a class.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of ground support capability (reduced load-bearing at one or more gear units)
fha.effAc: Reduced ground load path; one gear unit or bogie unable to carry its share, increasing footprint pressure on remaining units and risk of surface penetration/rutting on a semi-prepared strip; potential asymmetry in ground handling.
fha.effCrew: Increased workload managing directional control and stopping on a degraded surface; possible abnormal handling cues.
fha.effPax: No passengers carried; hold unoccupied in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Function definition supports stating a degraded ground load path, but the outcome (safe stop within margin vs runway excursion/structural overload) depends on how much support is lost, on which unit, and on the flotation margin of the semi-prepared surface — none of which the function definition alone fixes. Cannot derive a single worst-case class without the degradation extent; leaving severity empty per abstention.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of ground support and flotation capability
fha.effAc: Aircraft cannot be supported on its gear; gear collapse or total flotation failure on ground contact leads to fuselage/structure contact with the surface, loss of controlled rollout and probable major structural damage.
fha.effCrew: Sudden loss of ground path control; crew unable to arrest an uncontrolled ground event; high injury exposure.
fha.effPax: No passengers carried; hold unoccupied in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Complete loss of ground support/flotation at landing on a 392 t / 318 t MLW freighter results in loss of the airplane through structural collapse and uncontrolled ground contact; classified Catastrophic ↔ Extremely Improbable (1e-9/fh). Derived from stated effect (loss of the airplane), not assumed. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Wheel braking erroneously applied against crew command (braking active when not commanded / opposing crew intent)
fha.effAc: Unintended braking during take-off ground roll degrades acceleration and can prevent reaching V1 in available distance; braking against crew command during rollout on a 1,800 m strip against ~1,080 m predicted rollout erodes the stopping margin and can induce asymmetry, tyre/brake overheat and directional upset.
fha.effCrew: Crew confronted with braking inconsistent with command; increased workload to detect, diagnose and counter; possible directional control demand.
fha.effPax: No passengers carried; hold unoccupied in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect direction depends on symmetry and magnitude: symmetric mild drag versus a hard asymmetric application during a high-energy ground roll drive very different outcomes (increased workload up to runway excursion / directional loss). The function definition does not fix the magnitude or symmetry, so a single worst-case §25.1309 class cannot be derived here; abstaining. Candidate range Major↔Hazardous pending the erroneous-application characterisation.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of ground wheel-braking deceleration
fha.effAc: No wheel-braking deceleration available on the ground. Rollout relies on reverse thrust (inboard engines only) and aerodynamic drag; predicted braked rollout is ~1,080 m against an 1,800 m requirement on a semi-prepared unmaintained strip, so loss of wheel braking removes the primary means of staying within the available landing distance. Overrun of the strip end is credible, more so on a rejected take-off at high weight.
fha.effCrew: High workload managing directional control and reverse thrust with no braking; may need to execute an overrun.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; flight crew only exposed to overrun consequences.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: On a strip whose stopping margin is ~1,080 m predicted against 1,800 m available, total loss of wheel braking on landing or a high-weight RTO makes an overrun credible, with potential loss of the airplane. Confirm against the braking/performance substantiation and the accumulator-supported emergency braking that partially offsets total loss. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Reduced braking with degraded stopping performance
fha.effAc: Braking effectiveness reduced but present; stopping distance increases, eroding the margin between the ~1,080 m predicted rollout and the 1,800 m available landing distance. Depending on the degree of degradation the aircraft may stop within the strip using reverse thrust and remaining braking, or approach the strip limit.
fha.effCrew: Increased workload; crew apply reverse thrust and maximum available braking and monitor remaining distance.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Severity depends on the amount of braking lost and the resulting stopping distance against the 1,800 m requirement, which the FHA-level function definition does not quantify. Left empty pending the braking-degradation performance case that establishes whether reduced braking stays within available distance (Major) or threatens an overrun (higher).. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Asymmetric braking across the wheel groups
fha.effAc: Uneven braking force between left and right wheel groups produces a yawing moment during the ground roll, tending to swing the aircraft off the runway centreline. On a semi-prepared strip of limited width, directional excursion toward the strip edge is credible, compounding any stopping-distance shortfall.
fha.effCrew: Increased workload countering the yaw with steering and rudder while decelerating; directional control task added to the stopping task.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect hinges on the magnitude of the braking asymmetry and the controllability/edge margin of the semi-prepared strip, neither quantified at aircraft-function level. Left empty pending the directional-control-on-the-ground substantiation; classify once the yaw authority versus asymmetry case is available.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Degraded braking effectiveness below crew-detection threshold
fha.effAc: Braking capability is reduced by an amount too small for the crew to perceive, so no compensating action (earlier braking, reverse thrust selection) is taken. Actual stopping distance exceeds the value the crew plan against, eroding the margin to the 1,800 m available distance without warning.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue normal braking technique unaware of the shortfall; discover the deficit only late in the rollout, if at all.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Undetected small degradation: severity depends on how much distance the below-threshold loss adds relative to the ~720 m nominal margin, which the function definition does not quantify. Left empty pending the performance case bounding the undetected shortfall.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Anti-skid regulation error not evident to the crew
fha.effAc: Anti-skid mis-regulates braking (locked or under-applied wheels) without crew awareness. On a semi-prepared, potentially low-friction surface, wheel lock risks tyre damage and loss of braking effectiveness, while under-application lengthens the stopping distance — either way eroding the margin to the 1,800 m available distance with no crew cue to compensate.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue normal braking unaware of the anti-skid error; no compensating action taken.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect on stopping distance and tyre integrity depends on the nature of the anti-skid error and the surface friction, neither quantified at this level. Left empty pending the anti-skid failure-effect analysis and its distance impact against the 1,800 m requirement.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Reduced nose-wheel steering authority or range (partial loss of directional control on the ground)
fha.effAc: Reduced steering authority; directional control on the ground maintained but with reduced margin, aided by rudder and differential braking; degraded ability to hold centreline on the semi-prepared strip
fha.effCrew: Crew compensates with pedals, tiller range and differential braking; increased workload during ground manoeuvring
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect grounded from the FCIM (reduced authority/range) but the model does not quantify residual steering authority versus the directional-control margin needed on a 1,800 m semi-prepared surface, so a class between Minor and Major cannot be derived. Severity left blank.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Nose cargo door indicated locked when not fully secured
fha.effAc: The nose visor forms the pressure boundary and part of the forward fuselage structural load path when closed; an unsecured door falsely indicated locked can fail the pressure boundary and forward load path in flight, leading to rapid depressurisation and potential loss of the airframe. A pressure interlock prevents opening while pressurised but does not create the false 'locked' indication.
fha.effCrew: False lock indication and take-off configuration check pass; crew unaware of the unsecured condition and take no action.
fha.effPax: No passengers carried; hold unoccupied in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: The door is a primary pressure boundary and forward-fuselage structural load path; failure in flight with a false secure indication defeats the crew's only means of catching the error and can result in loss of the airplane. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Incomplete nose door lock engagement not detected by either sensing path
fha.effAc: Both dissimilar sensing paths (proximity harness and mechanical indicator linkage) fail to detect incomplete pin engagement; the visor pressure boundary and forward structural load path are compromised in flight without any indication, leading to potential rapid depressurisation and loss of the airframe.
fha.effCrew: Neither sensing path annunciates; crew have no indication and take no action.
fha.effPax: No passengers carried; hold unoccupied in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Silent loss of both independent lock-sensing paths on a door that is a primary pressure boundary and structural load path removes the last defence against undetected incomplete lock; in-flight failure can result in loss of the airplane. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Degraded or slowed loading/unloading access to the hold
fha.effAc: Loading/unloading of the blade is slowed or impaired; no in-flight effect (door cannot be operated in flight and hold is unoccupied).
fha.effCrew: Increased ground/turnaround workload and time; no flight-crew task effect in flight.
fha.effPax: None (hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only).
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Loading access is a ground operation with no stated in-flight aircraft, crew or occupant effect; the function definition supports no §25.1309-classifiable in-flight condition. Turnaround/dispatch impact requires operational-impact substantiation, not a safety class. Severity abstained.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of hold loading/unloading access
fha.effAc: Blade cannot be loaded or unloaded; aircraft cannot perform its mission but no in-flight aircraft effect (door not operable in flight, hold unoccupied).
fha.effCrew: Ground operation prevented; no in-flight flight-crew effect.
fha.effPax: None (hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only).
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Total loss of loading access is a ground/dispatch condition with no stated in-flight aircraft, crew or occupant effect; the function definition supports no §25.1309-classifiable failure condition. Mission-availability impact is not a safety severity. Severity abstained.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of tension at a single strap station
fha.effAc: Loss of tension on one strap; the SDD states load paths are sized such that the loss of any one strap is carried by its neighbours, so restraint of the blade is retained.
fha.effCrew: Loss of tension on any strap is annunciated in flight; crew has indication only with no in-flight adjustment.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The function definition states a single lost strap is carried by neighbouring load paths, so restraint is retained; the residual aircraft effect (reduced restraint margin) is not quantified by the function alone. Needs the restraint-margin / structural substantiation to establish an aircraft effect before a class can be derived — abstaining rather than defaulting to the benign end.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Restraint degradation outside the tension-loop coverage
fha.effAc: Restraint degradation in a region not instrumented by the tension monitoring loop; the aircraft effect depends on how much restraint capability is lost and where, which is not established by the function definition.
fha.effCrew: The single instrumented tension loop does not cover this degradation, so it is not annunciated; crew continues normally, unaware.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The extent of restraint capability lost outside tension-loop coverage, and hence the CG/structural effect, is not determined by the function definition. Loop-coverage scope and the load-path substantiation are needed to establish an aircraft effect and derive a class — abstaining.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous conditioning or pressurisation control response
fha.effAc: Pressurisation/conditioning control drives an incorrect response (erroneous cabin/hold differential or conditioning); positive and negative pressure relief valves protect the structure independently of the control system, bounding the structural excursion, but the resulting differential and its effect on the pressure vessel depend on the hold differential schedule, which is preliminary.
fha.effCrew: Erroneous control response is annunciated; crew can select manual mode / pneumatic backup and reconfigure.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight deck held at a conventional cabin altitude, so the occupied-compartment effect is via the flight-deck conditioning zone.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The hold pressurisation differential is explicitly preliminary and unfrozen, so the pressure-vessel effect that drives severity for an erroneous control response is not fixed; independent mechanical relief bounds but does not define the effect. A frozen hold-differential schedule is needed to derive the class — abstaining.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous differential control developing below detection threshold
fha.effAc: Erroneous pressure-differential control develops slowly below the detection/annunciation threshold; the crew take no action, so the differential can drift toward the relief-valve settings before it is either bounded by independent mechanical relief or detected. The magnitude of the excursion and its effect on the pressure vessel depend on the preliminary hold differential schedule.
fha.effCrew: Below the detection threshold and unannunciated; crew continue normal duties and take no action regarding it.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; occupied-compartment effect is via the flight-deck conditioning zone.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect turns on the unfrozen hold differential schedule and on the detection-threshold and relief-valve settings, none of which the function definition fixes; the pressure-vessel excursion driving severity is therefore not established — abstaining rather than reaching for a value.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of air conditioning and distribution to occupied compartments
fha.effAc: Loss of flight-deck conditioning and distribution; aircraft altitude-limited to FL260; forced descent to a survivable pressure/temperature environment likely required.
fha.effCrew: Increased workload managing a descent/diversion; crew fall back on demand oxygen (system sized for the diversion time at max operating altitude) for smoke/fume or loss-of-conditioning cases.
fha.effPax: Hold is unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Flight-deck conditioning loss forces a descent/diversion with increased crew workload but with crew oxygen available and a low maximum operating altitude — significant reduction in safety margin / significant workload increase. Proposed only; the depressurisation-rate and time-of-useful-consciousness case that could drive Hazardous is not derivable from the SDD. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Reduced conditioning capacity or single-zone loss
fha.effPax: Hold is unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — 'Reduced' capacity is not quantified and single-pack operation is explicitly permitted with a reduced hold conditioning schedule, so residual capability cannot be established from the SDD. Cannot classify without a defined degradation level and its effect on the flight-deck environment.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of pressure-differential control within limits
fha.effPax: Hold is unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — 'Within limits' means no structural or physiological exceedance is stated, so no aircraft, crew or occupant effect is derivable from the SDD. Cannot classify without a quantified deviation and its consequence.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Slow loss of pressurisation differential below crew-detection threshold
fha.effPax: Hold is unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The SDD gives no depressurisation rate, no floor value, and no crew-exposure/time-of-useful-consciousness model, so neither the crew nor the structural effect of an undetected slow loss can be grounded. Cannot classify without that rate and threshold data.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous over-pressurisation of the occupied compartment
fha.effAc: Erroneous over-pressurisation schedule; positive/negative pressure relief valves protect the structure independently of the control system, capping the differential excursion.
fha.effCrew: Increased workload to select manual pressurisation mode and manage the excursion; erroneous differential annunciated via cabin-altitude/differential indication.
fha.effPax: Hold is unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Independent mechanical relief limits the over-pressure so structural rupture is precluded by design, leaving a significant workload increase / margin reduction — proposed Major. True severity depends on the relief-valve setting versus the structural limit, which the SDD does not quantify; confirm against structural substantiation. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of pressure differential control
fha.effAc: Fuselage differential no longer actively controlled; independent mechanical positive/negative relief still protects the structure. Occupied flight deck subject to an uncontrolled cabin-altitude excursion toward ambient at the low operating flight levels.
fha.effCrew: Crew must recognise the loss, don oxygen masks (quick-donning, four stations available) and initiate an emergency descent/diversion.
fha.effPax: No passengers carried; hold is unoccupied in flight — not applicable.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effects on the occupied flight deck stated, but the maximum uncontrolled cabin altitude reachable at the operating flight levels, the excursion rate, and the crew-oxygen diversion margin are not quantified in the SDD at aircraft level; cannot derive Hazardous vs Catastrophic without the occupied-compartment altitude limit. Severity abstained.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Reduced control of pressure differential
fha.effAc: Differential control degraded but still partially available; independent mechanical relief remains as a structural backstop. Occupied flight deck exposed to a reduced or drifting cabin-altitude schedule.
fha.effCrew: Crew manage a degraded pressurisation schedule, monitor cabin altitude, and may elect a lower cruise level or descent.
fha.effPax: No passengers carried; hold is unoccupied in flight — not applicable.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Degraded-control effects stated, but the achievable cabin-altitude band under partial control and the associated exposure are not quantified in the SDD; cannot derive Major vs Minor for the occupied compartment without that data. Severity abstained.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of automatic control with manual reversion available
fha.effAc: Automatic differential control lost; a pneumatic/manual backup mode is available to maintain differential on a single outflow valve. Fuselage differential maintainable by crew action.
fha.effCrew: Crew revert to manual pressurisation control; increased workload to schedule and monitor cabin altitude manually for the remainder of the flight.
fha.effPax: No passengers carried; hold is unoccupied in flight — not applicable.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — A manual/pneumatic backup mode is documented, so this is a workload-and-reversion condition rather than a loss of differential; but the cabin-altitude behaviour and residual margin achievable on manual reversion, and the workload increment, are not stated at aircraft level. Cannot derive Major vs Minor without that. Severity abstained.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous under-pressurisation of the occupied compartment
fha.effAc: Control drives the occupied compartment to a lower-than-scheduled differential (higher cabin altitude) contrary to the intended schedule, while control still operates. Independent negative-pressure relief protects the structure but does not restore the intended cabin altitude.
fha.effCrew: Crew exposed to an elevated cabin altitude; recognition depends on cabin-altitude indication and alerting, followed by oxygen use and descent.
fha.effPax: No passengers carried; hold is unoccupied in flight — not applicable.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Erroneous-low-differential effect on the occupied compartment stated, but the maximum cabin altitude the erroneous schedule can command and the resulting physiological exposure/time are not quantified in the SDD; the occupied-compartment altitude limit that would fix the class is not given. Severity abstained.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous pressure differential schedule developing below detection thresholds
fha.effAc: An erroneous differential schedule develops slowly, below the detection/alerting threshold; the excursion is not annunciated. Occupied compartment reaches an off-schedule cabin altitude with the crew unaware.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue normal duties and take no action regarding the condition (unaware case); no recognition until the excursion crosses a detection or physiological threshold, if at all.
fha.effPax: No passengers carried; hold is unoccupied in flight — not applicable.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Unaware slow-excursion effects stated with no assumed crew action, but the cabin altitude reachable before any threshold is crossed, and the physiological exposure at that altitude, are not quantified in the SDD; the occupied-compartment altitude limit is not given. Severity abstained.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous bleed ice-protection activation reducing available capacity when not required
fha.effAc: Bleed drawn for anti-ice when not required reduces bleed available to the ECS packs (shared cross-bleed manifold) and imposes an aerodynamic/performance penalty; the performance penalty is applied automatically to the displayed performance. Undetected inflight demand degrades pack capacity and thrust margin.
fha.effCrew: Crew observe IPS-in-use status and reduced pack capacity; may reconfigure bleed/pack schedule.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect is a reduction in available bleed/performance capacity, but the SDD does not quantify the margin lost or whether a single-side spurious demand crosses a safety-margin threshold; cannot derive a class without the ECS/performance margin data. Severity left empty pending engineering data.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of ice protection on protected aerodynamic surfaces and inlets
fha.effAc: Ice protection available on some but not all protected wing/inlet surfaces in the icing envelope; ice accretion on an unprotected leading-edge or inlet segment degrades lift/drag and inlet flow with a reduction in safety margins whose magnitude depends on icing severity at encounter.
fha.effCrew: Lost zone annunciated (electrical) or reduced bleed protection evident; crew exit icing conditions and may manually select the system on.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The condition is a partial loss with a safety-margin reduction, but its magnitude (MAJ vs HAZ) depends on the icing severity assumed at encounter and the aerodynamic penalty of the affected segment, neither of which the SDD quantifies. Cannot derive the class without that judgement; severity left empty.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected loss of ice protection on a protected surface or inlet
fha.effAc: With loss undetected, ice accretes on a protected surface or inlet while the crew continue normal duties and take no action; unmitigated accretion in the icing envelope produces a progressive reduction in lift/drag or inlet flow up to a large reduction in safety margins.
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware and take no corrective action (no exit from icing, no manual selection); first cue may be handling degradation.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Unaware case: the crew take no action, which routinely worsens severity, but the aircraft outcome (whether accretion on the affected surface reaches a hazardous handling/performance state) depends on icing severity and the aerodynamic sensitivity of the surface, which the SDD does not quantify. Cannot derive the class; severity left empty.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous electrical heating activation reducing available electrical capacity
fha.effAc: Electrical stabiliser/probe/windshield heating energised when not required draws electrical capacity that is then unavailable to other consumers; the significance depends on the electrical margin, which is not visible at aircraft-function level.
fha.effCrew: Crew observe IPS status; may deselect. Bus/load data available on the avionics.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect is a reduction in available electrical capacity, but whether a spurious heating demand crosses a safety-margin threshold depends on the EPS generation/bus margin, which the AFHA cannot see and the SDD does not quantify. Cannot derive the class; severity left empty.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of electrical ice protection across heated zones and elements (stabilisers, probes, ports, windshields)
fha.effAc: Reduced ice-protection coverage on a subset of monitored elements; remaining zones/elements protected. Where a heated probe or static port is affected, air-data quality on that source may degrade in icing; stabiliser leading-edge protection reduced in one or more of six zones.
fha.effCrew: Lost zone is annunciated (heating zones and elements are individually monitored); crew restricts to non-icing conditions or exits icing, cross-checks air-data sources, increased monitoring workload.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground a single class: the aircraft effect spans from a single stabiliser zone (annunciated, benign) to a heated probe/port loss corrupting one air-data source, and the SDD does not state how many/which elements a 'partial' loss covers nor the air-data redundancy margin remaining. Needs engineering scoping of which elements are in the partial set before a class is derived.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of electrical ice protection on stabilisers, probes, static ports and windshields
fha.effAc: In icing, ice accretes on empennage leading edges (pitch/yaw handling degraded), and heated pitot/static/AoA and windshield protection is lost — multiple air-data sources can ice simultaneously and windshield vision degrades. Wing/inlet bleed anti-ice is a separate function and remains, but tail and air-data protection is gone.
fha.effCrew: Loss annunciated; crew must exit icing immediately, manage degraded handling and potentially misleading/lost air data across sources, and cope with reduced forward vision — high workload in a demanding regime.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Simultaneous loss of empennage ice protection and heated air-data/windshield elements in icing gives a large reduction in safety margins and handling capability with high crew workload; multiple iced air-data sources can defeat voting. Derived from the stated effects, not assumed. To confirm against the icing exposure and air-data redundancy before commit. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of primary flight, navigation and system information (crew aware)
fha.effAc: Reduced primary information available; remaining aircraft effect depends on which information is lost and whether independent standby coverage remains
fha.effCrew: Increased crew workload managing a degraded information set; extent of workload and reversion depends on the specific loss
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The FC text states only 'partial loss' and does not identify which information is lost or whether the independent standby instrument remains available; without that the effect swings between Major and Hazardous, so severity is left blank pending scope of the partial loss.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous alert presented to the crew by the consolidated crew alerting
fha.effAc: Aircraft effect depends on the crew response the erroneous alert induces; a false alert may prompt an unnecessary or inappropriate procedure or configuration change
fha.effCrew: Crew presented with an alert and associated procedure for a condition that does not exist; potential distraction, unnecessary workload, or an inappropriate action taken in response
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — A single erroneous alert can range from a nuisance (slight workload increase) to a mis-diagnosis that drives an inappropriate crew action with a significant safety consequence; the FC text does not bound which alert or the induced action, so severity is left blank pending that scope and the assumed crew response.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of crew alerting consolidation and presentation
fha.effAc: No consolidated alerting is available; no system condition is annunciated or accompanied by its associated procedure. The aircraft remains controllable but any concurrent or subsequent failure proceeds without alerting prompt.
fha.effCrew: Crew receives no consolidated alerts or procedures and must detect and diagnose all conditions from individual indications, substantially increasing workload during any concurrent failure.
fha.effPax: No occupants in hold; not applicable.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effects support at least Major, but classifying complete loss of consolidated alerting as Hazardous versus Major depends on the crew-workload assessment under concurrent failures and on what independent indication survives — neither the crew-workload analysis (against the HIDH 80% time-occupancy line and the AC 25.1309 workload-severity ladder) nor the set of retained independent indications is established in the SDD. Severity left empty pending that analysis rather than defaulting to a plausible class.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of fire/overheat/smoke detection in one or more monitored zones (annunciated)
fha.phases: Taxi, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Detection is unavailable in one or more monitored zones; a fire or overheat in an affected zone would not be detected. Loss is annunciated, allowing the crew to account for the reduced coverage; remaining zones retain detection.
fha.effCrew: Crew alerted to loss of detection coverage in the affected zone(s); increased vigilance and a dispatch/coverage decision required; procedure for degraded detection applied.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect on the aircraft depends on WHICH zone loses coverage (an engine/APU fire zone versus a bleed-duct or gear-bay overheat zone) and on how much annunciated loss reduces the safety margin against an undetected fire — the function definition does not resolve which zone or how many, so the worst-case class cannot be committed. Confirm the zone scope and whether annunciation plus remaining coverage keeps this Major or drives it higher.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of detection in bleed-duct and gear-bay overheat coverage
fha.phases: Taxi, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Overheat detection on the bleed duct runs and in the main gear bays is unavailable; a bleed duct overheat/leak or a gear-bay overheat (e.g. brake overheat) would not be annunciated. Bleed-duct overheat left undetected can damage adjacent structure and systems along the wing-root run; gear-bay overheat undetected can progress unchecked.
fha.effCrew: No overheat warning for the affected zones; crew unaware of a developing bleed-duct or brake overheat; reduced ability to isolate the bleed source or manage a hot brake condition.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Overheat (not fire) in bleed-duct and gear-bay zones is a lower-energy hazard than an engine/APU fire, but the SDD does not state the consequence severity of an undetected bleed-duct or gear-bay overheat, so the aircraft effect cannot be firmly bounded to a class. Confirm whether an undetected bleed-duct overheat can damage the wing-root run / pressure boundary and whether gear-bay overheat is independently protected before classifying.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of fire, overheat and smoke detection along the hold (one or more monitored hold zones)
fha.effAc: An in-hold fire or smoke event in an affected zone is not detected; the hold carries no suppression, so early crew awareness is the only mitigation and it is lost for that zone. Undetected fire may progress in an unoccupied hold before any other indication reaches the crew.
fha.effCrew: No alert for a developing hold fire in the affected zone; crew continue normally and lose the diversion/response time that early detection would have given.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect. Flight crew only aboard.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect hinges on whether an undetected in-hold fire in a partially-covered, unsuppressed hold can progress to a hazardous or catastrophic outcome before other cues appear — a fire-progression / hold-fire substantiation not present in the SDD (which records the no-suppression decision as an assumption to be substantiated). Cannot derive the class without that; left empty.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected degradation of a fire/overheat/smoke detection loop below the warning threshold, no fault indication to the crew
fha.effAc: A detection loop degrades silently so that a genuine fire, overheat or smoke event in the affected zone would not raise a warning; the loss of protection is itself not annunciated, so the crew believe detection remains available.
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware detection is compromised; no maintenance or dispatch action taken; a subsequent real event in the affected zone goes unwarned.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect. Flight crew only aboard.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Severity depends on the outcome of an unwarned fire/overheat in the affected zone and on the dual-loop degraded-logic coverage — the SDD states dual-loop AND logic degrading to single-loop but does not establish the residual coverage of a below-threshold degradation, nor the consequence of an unwarned event. Cannot derive the class; left empty.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of fire, overheat and smoke detection across all monitored zones
fha.effAc: No detection of fire or overheat in any monitored zone — engine nacelles, APU, bleed ducts, main gear bays and the hold. A fire in any zone (including engine/APU fire zones) develops with no warning; crew cannot arm the correct extinguisher response because they are unaware of the event.
fha.effCrew: No fire/overheat alerting for any zone; crew fly on unaware of a developing fire until a secondary, later cue (thrust loss, smoke ingress, control effect) appears, by which point margins are much reduced.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; flight crew only aboard. No occupant effect until the underlying fire produces an aircraft-level consequence.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Total loss of detection across all fire zones removes the only means by which the crew becomes aware of, and responds to, a fire in high-energy flammable-fluid zones (engine nacelles, APU); an undetected engine/APU fire progressing without response can lead to loss of the aircraft. Proposed Catastrophic for engineer confirmation, worst-phase across applicable phases. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Inadvertent extinguishant discharge into an engine or APU zone with no fire present
fha.effAc: Extinguisher bottle for an engine pair discharged with no fire; with two bottles per pair cross-plumbed, agent is expended and remaining protection for that pair is reduced. No direct thrust or control effect from the discharge itself; the loss is the reduced availability of extinguishing for a subsequent real fire in that pair.
fha.effCrew: Crew respond to a false-discharge indication; nuisance event, some workload to confirm no fire and manage remaining agent; dispatch/continued-flight decision affected.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; flight crew only aboard. No direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Single inadvertent discharge with no fire causes no immediate aircraft effect and a slight increase in crew workload; residual protection remains via the cross-plumbed second bottle of the pair. Proposed Minor for confirmation. If the discharge itself were shown to affect the running engine, this would need re-classification — not supported by the SDD, so held at Minor. [anchor MIN-2 — Minor] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Failure to discharge extinguishant on crew command into an engine or APU zone with a fire present
fha.effAc: Crew commands the fire handle for a detected engine or APU fire and the agent does not discharge; the fire in a high-energy, flammable-fluid fire zone is not suppressed and continues to progress with the primary means of extinguishing lost.
fha.effCrew: Crew have detected the fire and initiated the correct response, but suppression does not occur; they must fall back on shutdown/fuel isolation and diversion while an unsuppressed fire develops.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; flight crew only aboard. Occupant effect follows from the aircraft-level outcome of an unsuppressed fire.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Loss of the extinguishing response to a confirmed engine/APU fire is a large reduction in safety margin, the fire being in a flammable-fluid fire zone; classified below TL-detection because the fire is detected and shutdown/isolation remain, but a single unsuppressed fire zone event does not by itself establish loss of the aircraft. Proposed Hazardous for confirmation; would move to Catastrophic if an unsuppressed nacelle/APU fire is shown to defeat containment. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of fire extinguishing in engine and APU zones
fha.effAc: With an in-zone fire present, no means to extinguish or suppress fire in any engine nacelle or the APU compartment; fire may propagate to adjacent structure, fuel, hydraulic and electrical services in the nacelle/aft fuselage fire zones.
fha.effCrew: Fire detection and warning remain; crew have fire handles/shut-off but no discharge effect; forced to rely on isolation and expedited diversion with an uncontrolled fire.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: An uncontrolled, unextinguishable fire in an engine nacelle or the APU fire zone can propagate to fuel/structure and lead to loss of the airplane. Contingent on a concurrent in-zone fire (see assumption). [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Reduced extinguishing capability in a protected zone
fha.effAc: With an in-zone fire present, extinguishing agent available but at reduced capability (e.g. degraded discharge or single bottle where two credited); may fail to knock down or fully suppress a developed fire, allowing continued or re-ignited burning in the affected fire zone.
fha.effCrew: Detection and warning available; crew discharge available but effectiveness reduced; workload of managing a partially-controlled fire and diversion.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect depends on how much extinguishing margin is lost and whether a single discharge remains sufficient against the credited fire, plus the assumed concurrent-fire scenario — neither the amount of impairment nor the residual suppression margin is fixed at aircraft-function level. Cannot derive severity without that.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of extinguishing to one engine or APU zone only
fha.effAc: With a fire in the affected zone, no discharge available to that single engine nacelle or the APU compartment while other zones remain protected; fire in that one zone is uncontrolled and may propagate to adjacent fuel/structure/services.
fha.effCrew: Detection and warning available for that zone; crew have fire handle and fuel shut-off (isolation) but no extinguishing effect in the affected zone; expedited diversion.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: An uncontrolled fire in an individual engine nacelle or the APU fire zone, with no extinguishing means for that zone, can propagate to fuel/structure and lead to loss of the airplane. Contingent on a concurrent fire in that zone (see assumption); the engineer should confirm whether isolation-only credit reduces this class. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected loss of agent charge before demand
fha.effAc: Extinguishing bottle(s) unavailable at demand without prior indication; on a subsequent in-zone fire the crew attempt discharge and it does not occur, leaving the fire uncontrolled.
fha.effCrew: No prior awareness of the lost charge; on discharge attempt the fire is not suppressed; late recognition and reliance on isolation and diversion.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Classification requires an assumed subsequent fire AND the crew being unaware of the lost charge at demand; whether a pressure/charge monitor and dispatch check make this detectable is not resolved at aircraft-function level. Without fixing the concurrent-fire context and the awareness state, the aircraft effect cannot be derived.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous or contaminated oxygen delivery on demand
fha.effAc: No direct effect on the airframe; oxygen is supplied to the flight crew for depressurisation, smoke and fume events and the ensuing diversion.
fha.effCrew: On demand (loss of pressurisation, smoke/fume), crew receive erroneous or contaminated breathing gas; potential incapacitation or impaired performance of both crew during the phase where oxygen is most needed.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Severity hinges on the assumed concurrent event that triggered oxygen demand (e.g. high-altitude depressurisation vs. ground smoke) and on how many crew stations are affected; the M condition statement fixes neither the triggering context nor the number of crew impaired. Crew incapacitation during a depressurisation could be Catastrophic, but that context must be confirmed before classifying.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of breathing oxygen supply to the crew
fha.effCrew: With no oxygen available, a coincident loss-of-pressurisation, smoke or fume event at up to FL260 leaves the crew unprotected; crew incapacitation from hypoxia or smoke/fume exposure is credible during the descent and diversion that follow such an event (SDD §5.13.1).
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Complete loss of the only crew protection against depressurisation/smoke/fume at up to FL260 removes a safety margin whose demand (a decompression or fume event) is itself a foreseeable condition; a large reduction in functional capabilities with potential crew distress. Whether this reaches Catastrophic depends on the coincident-event exposure and time-of-useful-consciousness at FL260, which the SDD does not quantify — engineer to confirm class. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Reduced oxygen availability to the crew
fha.effCrew: Reduced availability shortens protected diversion time; the system is sized for four occupants for the diversion associated with the maximum operating altitude, with reserve (SDD §5.13.2), so a reduction erodes that reserve and may curtail a diversion or force an earlier descent, increasing crew workload during a depressurisation/fume event.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground the magnitude of the reduction from the function definition: the effect depends on how much reserve remains versus the required diversion time and whether the reduced supply still covers a worst-case diversion at FL260 — none of which the SDD quantifies. Severity left blank rather than guessing a mid-scale value.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of supply to a single mask station
fha.effCrew: One of the four mask stations is without oxygen; with a nominal complement of two and provision for four (SDD §1.1/§5.13.2), the affected station may or may not be occupied. Regulators are independent per mask (SDD §5.13.3), so remaining stations are unaffected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify from the function definition alone: the effect turns on whether the affected station is a required crew position and whether an unaffected station is available for that crew member. The SDD gives four mask stations and independent regulators but does not fix which station this condition strikes. Severity left blank.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Failure to deliver oxygen on crew donning action
fha.effCrew: The crew, believing they are protected, don a mask that delivers no oxygen during a depressurisation, smoke or fume event; unlike a total loss the failure may be discovered only on demand, so the crew are exposed without warning during the very event the system exists to protect against (SDD §5.13.1/§5.13.6, masks donned on crew action, no automatic deployment).
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: A delivery failure that manifests on demand denies protection at the moment of need and may not be evident until the event, so no compensating crew action is available; a large reduction in functional capability with potential crew distress. As with the TL row, whether this reaches Catastrophic depends on coincident-event exposure and time-of-useful-consciousness at FL260, which the SDD does not quantify — engineer to confirm class. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected degradation of delivered oxygen quality
fha.effCrew: Delivered oxygen is contaminated or of degraded quality without annunciation; cylinder pressure and low-pressure alerting are provided (SDD §5.13.4) but quality is not monitored, so the crew breathe a degraded supply during a depressurisation/fume event believing it adequate, with potential subtle impairment.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground the aircraft/crew consequence severity: the effect depends on the nature and degree of quality degradation (e.g. contaminant, partial-pressure shortfall) and the resulting crew impairment, none of which the function definition or SDD characterises. The SDD indicates pressure/low-pressure alerting but no quality monitoring; the physiological effect is unquantified here. Severity left blank rather than reaching for a value.. Engineer to classify.

assumptions.text: The worst-case asymmetric thrust source for SF-001 malfunction and partial-loss conditions is an outboard engine at the 28 m (0.35 semi-span) moment arm.
assumptions.rationale: The FHA must classify by worst effect but the SDD does not tabulate per-engine asymmetry effects; the outboard moment arm is the stated directional-control sizing case, so it is taken as the driving position.
assumptions.ifWrong: If an inboard or combined case drives the worst asymmetry differently, the Hazardous/Catastrophic proposals for SF-001-M, SF-001-M2 and SF-001-PL2 could shift.

citations.quote: The outboard engine moment arm is 28 m, taken as 0.35 of the 80 m semi-span

assumptions.text: Single-engine partial loss remains within available directional-control authority in all applicable phases (i.e. SF-001-PL is bounded by the design dispatch case).
assumptions.rationale: The severity split between PL (Major) and PL2 (Catastrophic) hinges on whether a given thrust loss stays within rudder authority; the SDD asserts one-engine-out continuation but does not quantify the authority boundary.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a single-engine outboard loss at a critical phase can exceed authority, SF-001-PL migrates toward Hazardous/Catastrophic.

citations.quote: designed to continue to a suitable aerodrome following the loss of any one engine at or after V1

assumptions.text: The hold is unoccupied in flight, so occupant effects are limited to the two-to-four flight crew for every SF-001 condition.
assumptions.rationale: Passenger/occupant effect columns require knowing who is aboard; the SDD states the hold is not occupied in flight.
assumptions.ifWrong: If occupants were carried in the hold, the occupant-effect column and possibly severities would change.
