assumptions.text: The hold is unoccupied in flight and only flight crew are exposed to any in-flight failure condition.
assumptions.rationale: Passenger-effect classification requires knowing who is aboard; the FHA effect-on-occupants field depends on it.
assumptions.ifWrong: If occupants were carried in flight, the occupant-effect column and possibly severity of every in-flight condition would change.

citations.quote: The aircraft carries flight crew only

assumptions.text: The 1,800 m semi-prepared landing distance requirement and ~1,080 m predicted rollout together define the ground-deceleration safety margin against which reverse-thrust losses are judged.
assumptions.rationale: The SF-002 ground conditions cannot be classified without the deceleration budget; the SDD gives the requirement and predicted rollout but not the braking-only rollout.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the braking-only rollout exceeds 1,800 m, SF-002-TL/PL would classify more severely; if well inside, less severely.

citations.quote: The margin between those two numbers is the operating margin on which the braking and flotation design rests.

assumptions.text: In-flight reverser deployment protections (WOW + radio-altimeter agreement + mechanical sleeve lock) are effective, so SF-002-M residual severity depends on failure of those protections and cannot be committed from the function level.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD states the in-flight inhibit; the FHA function definition does not establish the post-protection controllability outcome.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the inhibits are not credited, SF-002-M could be a committed Hazardous/Catastrophic loss-of-control condition rather than an abstention.

citations.quote: with a mechanical lock at the translating sleeve.

assumptions.text: On the landing sizing case, reverse thrust is a material contributor to stopping distance such that its unannunciated loss meaningfully erodes the margin between the 1,800 m requirement and the ~1,080 m predicted rollout.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD gives the requirement and predicted rollout but not the split between wheel-braking and reverse-thrust contribution, forcing an assumption about how much of the margin depends on reversers.
assumptions.ifWrong: If reverse thrust contributes negligibly to the stopping case, SF-002-TL2 drops toward Minor/No Safety Effect; if it is a large contributor on a degraded surface, the row moves toward Hazardous.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-002-TL2 effAc and the deferred severity

citations.quote: The landing distance requirement is 1,800 m (6,000 ft) on such a surface. Predicted landing rollout at maximum landing weight is approximately 1,080 m.

assumptions.text: Thrust reversers are fitted to the two inboard engines only, so the reverse-thrust deceleration available is inherently partial relative to a four-reverser installation.
assumptions.rationale: The magnitude of the deceleration lost in SF-002-TL2 depends on the reverser fit, which the SDD states as inboard-only.
assumptions.ifWrong: If reversers were fitted to all four engines, the deceleration deficit on loss would be larger and the severity of SF-002-TL2 would tend more severe.

citations.quote: Thrust reversers are fitted to the two inboard engines only.

assumptions.text: The hold is unoccupied in flight and the aircraft carries flight crew only, so passenger effects are not applicable to any of these conditions.
assumptions.rationale: Occupant-effect classification depends on who is aboard; the SDD states no in-flight hold occupants.
assumptions.ifWrong: If occupants were carried in the hold, occupant-injury effects would enter the assessment and could raise severities on several rows.
assumptions.usedFor: effPax on all rows in this turn

assumptions.text: The hold is unoccupied in flight and the aircraft carries flight crew only, so no passenger-injury severity path applies to these conditions.
assumptions.rationale: The failure conditions require an occupant-effect column; the provided functions list gives no occupancy, so occupancy was taken from the SDD mission description.
assumptions.ifWrong: If occupants were carried in flight, the occupant-effect column and possibly the severity of SF-003-PL/PL2/TL would change.

assumptions.text: 'Beyond controllable limits' for SF-003-PL2 means the retained authority cannot maintain controlled flight.
assumptions.rationale: The condition label itself defines the boundary; the effect and severity were derived from that wording rather than from a controllability analysis in the inputs.
assumptions.ifWrong: If 'beyond controllable limits' is intended as a recoverable degraded state, SF-003-PL2 would drop from Catastrophic toward Hazardous.

assumptions.text: The hold is unoccupied in flight, so occupant effects are limited to the flight crew for every SF-004 and SF-005 condition.
assumptions.rationale: The FHA requires an effect-on-occupants entry; the SDD states the hold is not occupied and the aircraft carries flight crew only, which I relied on to null the passenger column.
assumptions.ifWrong: If any occupant is carried in the hold in flight, the occupant effect and hence the severity of the high-lift and ground-support conditions would need reassessment upward.
assumptions.usedFor: effPax on SF-004-M3, SF-004-PL, SF-004-TL, SF-005-M, SF-005-M2

citations.quote: The hold is not occupied in flight. The aircraft carries flight crew only

assumptions.text: High-lift failure conditions bind at low-speed phases (takeoff, approach, landing) where high-lift is required, and severity is taken as the worst applicable phase.
assumptions.rationale: ARP4761A requires classifying per phase then taking the worst; the SDD frames high-lift as 'high-lift for low-speed flight' but does not enumerate phase-by-phase effects, so I assigned the phases where the function is demanded.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a more critical phase applies (e.g. balked landing / go-around configuration change), the SF-004-PL/TL severities could rise.
assumptions.usedFor: phases and severity on SF-004-M3, SF-004-PL, SF-004-TL

citations.quote: Provide high-lift for low-speed flight

assumptions.text: The 1,800 m semi-prepared landing requirement against ~1,080 m predicted rollout is the governing margin for judging high-lift-degradation severity.
assumptions.rationale: No independent low-speed performance data was provided; the landing-distance margin is the only quantified low-speed constraint in the SDD and I used it to reason about margin reduction for partial and total high-lift loss.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the actual degraded-configuration landing performance still fits within the requirement with margin, SF-004-PL could drop below Major and SF-004-TL below Hazardous.

citations.quote: landing distance requirement of 1,800 m (6,000 ft), semi-prepared. Predicted landing rollout ... approximately 1,080 m

assumptions.text: No passengers are carried in flight, so occupant effect is limited to the flight crew.
assumptions.rationale: The FHA occupant column needs a passenger population; the SDD states the hold is unoccupied in flight and only flight crew are carried.
assumptions.ifWrong: If any occupant travels in the hold in flight, the occupant-effect column and potentially the severity of SF-005-TL and the braking rows would need re-evaluation for occupant injury.
assumptions.usedFor: effPax on SF-005-PL, SF-005-PL2, SF-005-TL, SF-006-M, SF-006-M2

citations.quote: The hold is not occupied in flight. The aircraft carries flight crew only

assumptions.text: Complete loss of ground support/flotation on landing results in loss of the airplane.

assumptions.text: The hold is unoccupied in flight and the aircraft carries flight crew only, so no passenger-oxygen failure condition exists and all Effect-on-Passengers fields are empty.
assumptions.rationale: The AFHA must state occupant effects; the SDD states there are no passengers in flight and no passenger oxygen, forcing the passenger-effect fields to be empty rather than analysed.
assumptions.ifWrong: If any occupant can be carried in the hold in flight, a passenger-oxygen protection gap becomes a new failure condition and the TL/M2 severities could rise.
assumptions.usedFor: effPax blanks on all SF-018 rows; severity of SF-018-TL and SF-018-M2

citations.quote: There is no passenger oxygen: the hold is not occupied in flight.

assumptions.text: Crew oxygen is demanded only in a coincident abnormal event (loss of pressurisation, smoke or fume) rather than in normal flight, so its failure severity is driven by exposure to that coincident event.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD defines the system's purpose as protection for those events; without a demand model the coincident-event exposure that sets whether TL/M2 are Hazardous or Catastrophic cannot be quantified here.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the demand rate or time-of-useful-consciousness at FL260 makes crew incapacitation near-certain on the event, SF-018-TL and SF-018-M2 could classify Catastrophic rather than Hazardous.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-018-TL and SF-018-M2 severity (Hazardous, HAZ-1) and their rationale hedges

citations.quote: supplies breathing oxygen to the flight crew for loss of pressurisation, smoke and fume events

assumptions.text: Maximum operating altitude is FL260 with a low-differential hold, so time-of-useful-consciousness on a depressurisation is longer than for a high-altitude transport but still safety-relevant.
assumptions.rationale: The severity of an oxygen-supply loss scales with cabin/hold altitude on decompression; the operating altitude bounds that, and the SDD fixes it at FL260 preliminary.
assumptions.ifWrong: If maximum operating altitude increases, the crew-effect severity of SF-018-TL/M2 worsens and could push toward Catastrophic.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-018-TL and SF-018-M2 crew effects and severity
